title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and thoroughly cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction
During the first trimester of pregnancy, nutrition plays a crucial role in the development of the fetus. Providing adequate nutrients helps prevent birth defects and ensures the health of both mother and baby. In this article, we will explore the essential factors in first-trimester nutrition, including folate, iron, and safer foods.

## Folate and its Importance
Folate is a critical nutrient during pregnancy, helping prevent birth defects such as neural tube defects. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), pregnant women should take 400 micrograms of folate daily. Foods rich in folate include leafy greens, fruits, whole grains, and dairy products.

## Iron and its Role
Iron is another essential nutrient during pregnancy, helping produce red blood cells and prevent anemia. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should take 27 milligrams of iron daily. Foods rich in iron include red meat, poultry, fish, beans, and nuts.

## Safer Foods
During the first trimester, pregnant women should avoid foods with a high risk of foodborne illness, such as:
* Raw or undercooked foods
* Foods containing listeria, such as soft cheeses and deli meats
* Foods containing mercury, such as shark and swordfish

Instead, pregnant women should prioritize thoroughly cooked foods, such as:
* Leafy greens and fruits
* Cooked meats and fish
* Whole grains and dairy products

## Hydration and Fluid Intake
Adequate hydration is essential during pregnancy, helping prevent issues like constipation and urinary tract infections. Pregnant women should drink at least 8 cups of water daily and avoid caffeinated and sugary drinks.

## Conclusion
First-trimester nutrition is crucial for ensuring the health of both mother and baby. Providing adequate nutrients, including folate, iron, and safer foods, helps prevent birth defects and ensures the healthy development of the fetus. Pregnant women should consult a [meal planner](/planner) to create a personalized and safe nutrition plan.

## When to Seek Help
If you have any questions or concerns about nutrition during pregnancy, consult your healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. They can help you create a personalized and safe nutrition plan.

## FAQs
* Q: Why is folate important during pregnancy?
A: Folate helps prevent birth defects such as neural tube defects.
* Q: How can I get enough iron during pregnancy?
A: You can get enough iron through iron-rich foods like red meat, poultry, fish, beans, and nuts.
* Q: What foods should I avoid during the first trimester?
A: You should avoid raw or undercooked foods, foods containing listeria and mercury.
